claim: The real, non-placeholder translated title card ('Twilight Syndrome' / 'Search Chapter', a translation of OP.STR's own closing katakana logo and the game's Japanese subtitle 探索編/Tansaku-hen) is correctly burned into OP.STR, survives the psxavenc re-encode and disc patch, and renders correctly during real live playback under the game's own logo.
context: The user directly clarified (2026-08-29) that OP.STR's opening movie has no spoken dialogue to translate -- 'אין כלום, רק את שם הפתיחה של המשחק בסוף' (there's nothing, just the game's opening title at the end). This supersedes subtitle_tracks/op_intro.json's 14 audio-activity-derived cues as a source of real dialogue content for THIS movie -- that track's RMS-based detection evidently picked up non-speech audio (music/sound effects), not spoken lines, and its 'TBD' placeholder text should not be treated as pending real dialogue. The only real translatable content in OP.STR is the title card itself, confirmed by direct inspection of the movie's own decoded frames (2274 total, 15fps, ~151.6s): a particle-assembly animation (starting ~frame 2015) that settles into a fully static hold of the katakana logo 'トワイライトシンドローム' from frame 2103 through the movie's last frame 2274 (~11.4s hold).
method: Located the title card's exact frame range by direct pixel-statistics inspection of the previously-decoded OP.STR frames (frame_02103 onward: mean/std become constant through frame_02274, confirming a fully static hold; verified visually).

Added `\n`-as-forced-line-break support to gcrts.burn_in_subtitle.wrap_text_to_width (each segment still independently word-wrapped) so an intentional two-line title ('Twilight Syndrome' / 'Search Chapter') renders as two clean lines rather than being auto-wrapped unpredictably -- 2 new unit tests added, full suite still green.
Created subtitle_tracks/op_title_card.json (t=140.2s, duration=11.47s, text='Twilight Syndrome\nSearch Chapter') as the real (non-placeholder) content track for this movie.
Ran gcrts.movie_subtitle_burner.build_burned_in_movie end-to-end against the real disc's OP.STR, burning this cue onto its frame range.

OFFLINE VERIFICATION: independently re-decoded the resulting .str file and confirmed the burned text renders as 2 clean lines directly beneath the original Japanese logo, at the correct frame position (a few frames of compression-rounding slack, consistent with prior findings) -- see offline_decoded_output_frame.png.
Patched into a disc image copy (op_title_card_demo.bin/.cue), loaded into a fresh PCSX-Redux instance via File > Open Disk Image, reset via PCSX.hardResetEmulator()+resumeEmulator().

LIVE VERIFICATION: polled gcrts.overlay_identity.identify_overlay() over live GDB to detect MOP.EXE residency, then ran one continuous, gapless 700-frame screenshot capture (0.3s interval, 210s total -- deliberately gapless this time after an earlier attempt with two separate capture windows missed the actual appearance window due to a coverage gap). Detected a sustained ~19-second bright-region transition at t=136.68s-155.60s in the video panel (vs. two isolated single-frame brightness blips elsewhere in the movie, correctly distinguished as unrelated bright scene-cuts, not the title card). Directly viewed a frame in the middle of that window: confirmed the real, translated title card rendering exactly as built.
Assembled a 17-frame GIF (title_card_proof.gif) spanning the clean footage immediately before the card through its settled, legible hold.
result: CONFIRMED_LIVE end-to-end: the real translated title card burns in correctly, survives re-encode/patch, and renders correctly during actual playback, both offline (exact frame bytes) and live (real emulator boot).

limitations_and_notes: A large per-boot delay before MOP.EXE became resident, and independently a large, apparently CD-streaming-related real-time stretch of the movie's own later portion, were both observed and are consistent with this project's already-documented finding that t_ref/real-time playback timing is NOT reliable to predict in advance for this disc -- empirical scanning (this time a continuous, gapless capture) was required, exactly as documented previously. A first attempt at live verification, using two separate capture windows with an unmonitored gap between them, missed the title card's appearance entirely and had to be redone gaplessly.

'waring:old type streaming mode in CdRead2' is a normal, pre-existing console message (also seen for MPRO.EXE in docs/renderer/MOVIE_LOADER_ARCHITECTURE.md), unrelated to this change. A separate 'Capture buffer is overflowing. Increase CB_SIZE.' warning was also observed in the logs during this session's live tests; it did not prevent correct playback and is suspected to be an unrelated leftover from an earlier SPU/audio capture debug feature, not investigated further since playback was confirmed correct.
